passages.note: Campaign policy page treats adult cannabis use as legal and proposes permits for age-restricted licensed lounges; this is on the legal side but states nothing about a taxed market or minimal restrictions, so it does not separate rung 4 from rung 5.
Mentions cannabis-tax funding only as an example of nonprofit spending; says nothing about what should be legal.

rows.reasoning: His only on-question words, "GIVE ADULTS LEGAL PLACES TO USE LEGAL CANNABIS INDOORS" with permits for "age-restricted licensed lounges and cafes", accept legal adult use and so rule out keeping cannabis illegal or medical-only. They do not state a "licensed, taxed commercial market" or treating cannabis as "an ordinary legal product, with minimal restrictions", so no rung on the legal side is established.
needs_source: Steve Hilton's own words (debate answer, questionnaire, or issue page) on how cannabis should be regulated, e.g. on the licensed, taxed adult-use market or on loosening cannabis-specific restrictions

quotes.text: The Office of Fun and Freedom will provide a ready-to-adopt local ordinance and a fast, coordinated permit for age-restricted licensed lounges and cafes, with worker ventilation protections, no alcohol and strict rules against impaired driving.
